record.tranche_reason: Compares a different training method with SGD and reports generalization performance, including an explicit training-versus-test comparison on MNIST.
record.gate_note: The paper reports DGB and SGD performance on natural-label benchmarks. Its batch sizes, architectures and learning rates vary across experiments, but the comparisons do not isolate batch size or architecture effects. Cited results about adaptive optimizers are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study compares DGB and normalized DGB with SGD, but its own results do not test any specified claim version. Adaptive-method disadvantages are cited from Wilson et al.; the experiments evaluate a new training method with tuning beyond learning rates and schedules. Generalization performance alone does not establish a test of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' conclusion: they present SGD as an implicitly regularized limiting case of DGB and conclude that DGB outperforms SGD on some tasks but underperforms when generalization requirements are stricter, illustrated by MNIST. More precisely, the derivation regularizes weight updates, and the image-recognition evidence is limited to one dataset.
record.recipe_differences: DGB fits layer-wise linear regressors to back-propagated pseudo-residuals; SGD is treated as its highly regularized extreme case. Experiments use ReLU networks and momentum 0.9.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that MNIST overfitting diminishes with larger α; NDGB's MNIST test performance approaches SGD. Performance also varies across datasets and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: DGB and NDGB outperform SGD on Higgs and Air, improve Reuters performance only marginally, and have no established advantage on HR given the reported variability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise gradient boosting can improve benchmark performance relative to SGD on some tasks, with benefits depending on the dataset and training configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, DGB converges faster on training data but has lower test accuracy than SGD. Raising α improves DGB test accuracy from 98.11% to 98.29%; SGD reaches 98.41%, and NDGB reaches 98.29%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DGB can trade faster training convergence for poorer held-out performance; stronger update regularization can reduce this disadvantage.

record.problems: Several tables report performance without identifying whether it is training or test performance. MNIST's train/test curves are figure-only without extractable values. The HR experiment's authors say its standard deviations are too large to claim DGB outperforms SGD.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result exceeding the 60-row limit; all benchmark performance entries and MNIST curve conditions are represented.

untested.parts: No fixed-random-label fitting or random-label held-out baseline paired with natural-label generalization.
No width sweep demonstrating zero training error and continued test-error improvement beyond that width.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No own comparison of the specified adaptive methods with SGD under limited tuning; their disadvantage is cited. DGB and NDGB experiments tune additional method and architecture parameters.
No reported controlled batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget or evaluation of recipes that remove a large-batch penalty.
No dropout intervention, small-training-set dropout comparison, or joint dropout and weight-decay removal.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measurement, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, retraining, or matched random-removal control.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain outside V1–V8; their states therefore cannot determine those versions. Tables 2–5 do not explicitly label their splits, although the test-convergence protocol and surrounding discussion indicate held-out evaluation. The record overstates split ambiguity for Table 6: the MNIST discussion identifies test performance and supplies numerical results. Benchmark results are useful for the separate claims in fits_no_version, but do not justify version verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization with the same architectures and recipes.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No adaptive optimizer comparison; DGB is the method compared with SGD.
No controlled large-batch comparison at fixed epoch budgets.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
